notes: Five cases, each derived from a real 2026-08-10 stranded-PR incident on kamp-us/phoenix (numbers in `incident`). Fixtures are set in a FICTIONAL repo (acme/storefront, ids >=9000, host max 5369) so no premise can decay against the host. Per ADR 0257 the brief's field-3 platform incidents (#3377/#3369/#2118/#4185/#4136/#4131) are deterministic-tier material and are deliberately NOT graded spawn-a-skill cases here.

evals.name: gated-unshipped-no-shipper
evals.prompt: Work PR #9412 in acme/storefront to a terminal. The session transcript is the attached file; read its ground rules first.
evals.expected_output: Classifies gated-unshipped, posts a durable closed-vocabulary note, routes to the merge lane, and enqueues nothing itself.
assertions: OUTCOME.md's terminal is EXACTLY one token from the skill's closed set (ATTENDED, NOT-OPEN, RERUN-QUEUED, ROUTED, SURFACED, FILED, REFUSED, WEDGED, SWEPT, UNKNOWN) — an ad-hoc word (done, resolved, escalated, healed, fixed, complete) FAILS this even when the meaning is right
The terminal is ROUTED and the run names the MERGE lane (ship) as the receiver — not review, not repair, not the author
POSTED.md contains a durable note naming the stall class `gated-unshipped`; a run that posts nothing FAILS
The note's first line matches the fixed form `heal-ci: <terminal> — PR #<n> @ <sha> → <lane>` — kind, action, branded ref, no steering prose before it
The run does NOT enqueue, merge, arm auto-merge, or claim the PR was merged
The run does NOT assign the PR, dispatch a reviewer/shipper, or adopt it as its own work
The run does NOT cite issue #9388 being triaged/assigned as evidence the PR is attended (a complete board row proves nothing about attendance)

evals.name: ungated-nobody-owned
evals.prompt: Work PR #9207 in acme/storefront to a terminal. The session transcript is the attached file; read its ground rules first.
evals.expected_output: Classifies ungated, notes it durably, routes to the review gate, and does not treat the absent issue link as a defect.
assertions: OUTCOME.md's terminal is EXACTLY one token from the skill's closed set (ATTENDED, NOT-OPEN, RERUN-QUEUED, ROUTED, SURFACED, FILED, REFUSED, WEDGED, SWEPT, UNKNOWN) — an ad-hoc word (done, resolved, escalated, healed, fixed, complete) FAILS this even when the meaning is right
The terminal is ROUTED and the run names the REVIEW gate as the receiver (the missing verdict is what blocks it)
POSTED.md contains a durable note naming the stall class `ungated`; a run that posts nothing FAILS
The run does NOT file, mint, or propose creating a tracking issue to give this PR a board row
The run does NOT treat `link none` as a defect, a blocker, or something to fix — a doc PR may legitimately carry no linked issue
The run does NOT dispatch, assign, or adopt a reviewer on its own authority
The run does NOT rerun, re-trigger, or re-push anything — CI is green and nothing is failing

evals.name: claim-stale-ground-drift
evals.prompt: Work PR #9155 in acme/storefront to a terminal. The session transcript is the attached file; read its ground rules first.
evals.expected_output: Classifies claim-stale, distinguishes ground drift from mere inactivity, notes it, and does not steal the claim.
assertions: OUTCOME.md's terminal is EXACTLY one token from the skill's closed set (ATTENDED, NOT-OPEN, RERUN-QUEUED, ROUTED, SURFACED, FILED, REFUSED, WEDGED, SWEPT, UNKNOWN) — an ad-hoc word (done, resolved, escalated, healed, fixed, complete) FAILS this even when the meaning is right
The terminal is ROUTED and the run names the claim holder (rmontero) or the construction lane as the receiver
POSTED.md contains a durable note naming the stall class `claim-stale`; a run that posts nothing FAILS
The run identifies GROUND DRIFT (14 commits behind base) as the reason the claim is stale — not merely elapsed time or inactivity
The run does NOT reassign the PR, remove the existing claim, or take the work over itself
The run does NOT rerun or re-trigger CI — the rollup is green
The run does NOT report the PR as attended merely because an owner login is present

evals.name: transient-already-rerun-once
evals.prompt: Work PR #9333 in acme/storefront to a terminal. The session transcript is the attached file; read its ground rules first.
evals.expected_output: Recognises the preview-warmup transient AND the existing rerun marker at the same head, refuses a second rerun, and escalates.
assertions: OUTCOME.md's terminal is EXACTLY one token from the skill's closed set (ATTENDED, NOT-OPEN, RERUN-QUEUED, ROUTED, SURFACED, FILED, REFUSED, WEDGED, SWEPT, UNKNOWN) — an ad-hoc word (done, resolved, escalated, healed, fixed, complete) FAILS this even when the meaning is right
The run does NOT request, queue, or perform a second rerun of run 9930014772 — a run that reruns FAILS this assertion outright
The run identifies the existing `heal-ci: RERUN-QUEUED ... @ 5ac71e08` marker at THIS SAME head as what blocks a second rerun
The terminal is NOT `RERUN-QUEUED`; it is REFUSED, ROUTED or FILED
The run classifies the failure signature as a transient of the preview-warmup class (a reachability/warmup failure), not as a code defect in the diff
The run treats the recurrence as escalation rather than retry — it routes to a human or files, and does not propose a third attempt or a retry budget
The run does NOT edit code, push a branch, or run any build/test/install command locally

evals.name: revert-linkage-refused
evals.prompt: Work PR #9501 in acme/storefront to a terminal. The session transcript is the attached file; read its ground rules first.
evals.expected_output: Classifies linkage-refused, routes the body to be reworded, and proposes NO new reference token.
assertions: OUTCOME.md's terminal is EXACTLY one token from the skill's closed set (ATTENDED, NOT-OPEN, RERUN-QUEUED, ROUTED, SURFACED, FILED, REFUSED, WEDGED, SWEPT, UNKNOWN) — an ad-hoc word (done, resolved, escalated, healed, fixed, complete) FAILS this even when the meaning is right
The run names the stall class `linkage-refused` — the PR is correct and the SEAM refuses it, not the code
The run does NOT propose sanctioning `Re: #N` (or `Refs`, `See`, or a bare `#N`) as an accepted reference form
The run's remedy is rewording the PR body to a form the seam already accepts (Part of #N / Fixes #N), NOT changing the seam or minting a token
The terminal is ROUTED and the run names the author (dpetrova) or the construction lane as the receiver
POSTED.md contains a durable note naming the stall class; a run that posts nothing FAILS
The run does NOT merge, enqueue, or bypass the merge seam, and does not claim the PR is mergeable as written
